benefits: Moves Excel data into XML-hungry systems: SOAP APIs, config importers and legacy software.
Custom root and row element names let the output match the schema your system requires.
Automatic escaping of &, < and > keeps every document well-formed.
Runs fully in the browser, so private spreadsheets are never uploaded.

faqs.a: Modern .xlsx files only. The old binary .xls format from Excel 2003 and earlier is not supported. Re-save such files as .xlsx first.
Dates are stored as serial numbers in Excel. This tool reads the stored value, so a date may appear as a number like 45658 rather than a formatted date.
faqs.q: Why do dates show as numbers?

faqs.a: The tool reads the workbook's sheet list and converts one worksheet at a time. Pick the sheet you need from the dropdown.
Only the stored cell values are converted. Formulas, charts and images are skipped; formula cells use their last saved values.
Header text is sanitized into valid XML names: spaces become underscores and illegal characters are removed. Empty headers become field1, field2 and so on.
faqs.q: How are messy header names handled?

howTo: Click Choose file and select an .xlsx workbook from your device.
Wait while the workbook is parsed in your browser.
Pick the worksheet you want from the dropdown.
Set the root element name and the row element name.
Press Download to save the .xml file, or Copy to paste it elsewhere.
keyFacts: Reads genuine .xlsx workbooks by parsing the ZIP container and sheet XML directly.
One row element per worksheet row; field elements come from the header row.
Root and row element names are fully customizable and validated as legal XML names.
Special characters are escaped automatically, so output always parses.
Choose any worksheet from a multi-sheet workbook before converting.

excel-to-xml.quickAnswer: Upload an .xlsx workbook and download any worksheet as well-formed XML. Each row becomes an element with child elements named after your headers, and you can customize the root and row tag names to match the schema your system expects.
excel-to-xml.tagline: Turn any Excel worksheet into clean, well-formed XML.
excel-to-xml.workedExample:
An .xlsx workbook has one worksheet, Products:
A1=Item, B1=Price
A2=Pen, B2=12.5

With root = products and row = product, the output is:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<products>
  <product>
    <Item>Pen</Item>
    <Price>12.5</Price>
  </product>
</products>

1 worksheet, 1 record, 2 fields converted to XML.
